The document "Sustainable Direct Recycling of Lithium-Ion Batteries via Solvent Recovery of Electrode Materials" (cssc-2020) states that the FTIR spectra of the delaminated cathode material show the characteristic peaks of pristine PVDF at 1,399, 1,180, and 870 cm^(−1), which are ascribed to the bending vibration of CH2, symmetrical stretching of CF2, and out-of-plane bending vibration of CH2, respectively. This suggests that the PVDF binder was not significantly dissolved or removed during the delamination process.

In fact, the FTIR spectra of the delaminated cathode material and the pristine PVDF binder are very similar, indicating that the PVDF binder remained intact during the delamination process.

Therefore, the answer is: essentially none of the PVDF binder was dissolved during delamination.
